Hand arithmetic: implied P(high) = 0.15*0.8 + 0.85*0.1 = 0.205 and 0.15*0.7 + 0.85*0.15 = 0.2325 (file prints 0.233, float rounding). Every derived percentage in README results 1-4 (47%/69%, 31%/52%, 14%/8%, 0.0066/0.0131, within 0.0009) recomputed from the table and matches. evidence.verification: `PYTHONPATH=src python3.13 -m pytest -q tests`: 7 passed in 0.11 s. Five seeded mutants via quality_mutate.py: naive prior from the wrong axis (caught), dropping the prior in value() (caught), blind baseline argmax->argmin (SURVIVED: blind is the reference for result 3 and the 'P(naive<blind)' columns, and no test checks it), speech utility sign 1-mask*noise -> 1+mask*noise in sim.py (SURVIVED: the utility model behind every number has no test at all), E-step A -> A.T (survived, but equivalent here because every test and experiment uses a symmetric uniform-error A; a non-symmetric auditor test would catch it). 2 of 4 non-equivalent mutants survive.
evidence.craft: Read est.py (88 lines), sim.py (121), run.py (71), test_est.py (57). Small, clear, vectorised; exact scoring under the true parameters rather than Monte Carlo of the policy value is the right choice; seeds are per-cell and naive/EM are scored on the same audit sets (paired). Defects: sim.py is a byte-identical copy (md5 8f33d938) shared by at least 14 ambient-* projects rather than a package; estimate_em returns silently at the iteration cap with no convergence flag (est.py:51-63); estimate_naive's default alpha=0 differs from the alpha=1 the experiments use (fine, but easy to misuse).
evidence.claims: Every number in the README is in results.txt and reproduces. The stylised-only disclaimer, AI-assistance note and a candid limitations list (known auditor matrix, independence, local optimiser, uniform errors) are present. Gaps: result 5's bold 'EM is not free at small n ... costs about what the bias does' rests partly on a mean difference of -0.0007 whose paired SE is 0.0005 (t = -1.35) and a 23% vs 21% rate within Monte Carlo error (~3 pp); the larger spread (0.0079 vs 0.0031) is real. No Monte Carlo SEs are reported anywhere. 'naive-implied label accuracy' is the unweighted mean of diag P(o|a) (run.py:35), which a reader will take for agreement P(o=a) (0.59 at label 0.7 / auditor 0.8, not 0.569). 'Next steps' list two items already done by ambient-dsaudit and ambient-goldaudit, not linked.
evidence.fitness: A researcher can build on it, and two follow-ups did (ambient-dsaudit, ambient-goldaudit cite it). But the result is the classical one: naive use of an imperfect reference standard gives biased sensitivity/specificity that does not vanish with n, and with the reference's error rates known the bias is removed by inversion (Gart and Buck 1966; Staquet et al. 1981; for classifier training, Natarajan et al. 2013 and Patrini et al. 2017 forward/backward correction). In the population limit the EM here is exactly that closed-form inversion (checked). The new part is only the translation into utility loss in a stylised round-number model with one mix and uniform errors; none of the literature on the core correction is cited, only Dawid-Skene from memory.
evidence.domain: Against standard latent-class practice: the known-matrix MLE by EM is correct and consistent, exact expected-utility scoring and the population-limit cell are the right design, paired seeds are good. Departures: no Monte Carlo standard errors for finite-n comparisons; only symmetric uniform-error matrices (so identifiability and asymmetric auditors are never exercised); misspecified auditor accuracy left untested although the auditor ran it in 10 population cells and found over-correction can make EM worse than naive (label 0.7, true auditor 0.9, assumed 0.7: EM 0.3877 vs naive 0.3904), which confirms the README's stated caveat.

defects.what: The blind baseline (reference for result 3 and the P(naive<blind) columns) and the whole utility model in sim.py have no test: argmax->argmin in blind and a sign flip in the speech utility both leave all 7 tests green. Tests also use only symmetric A, so an A/A.T slip in the E-step is invisible.

The core result (naive use of a noisy reference gives n-independent bias; with the reference's error matrix known, inversion/EM removes it) is the classical imperfect-reference-standard correction (Gart and Buck 1966; Staquet et al. 1981) and known-transition noisy-label correction (Natarajan et al. 2013; Patrini et al. 2017); none is cited, and in the population limit the EM is exactly the closed-form A^-T J inversion. Only the utility translation is new.

Result 5 says EM's small-n cost is 'about what the bias does' on a mean difference of -0.0007 (paired SE 0.0005, t=-1.35) and 23% vs 21% below blind (within MC error); no Monte Carlo SEs are reported anywhere. The spread difference is real.
'naive-implied label accuracy' is the unweighted mean of diag P(o|a), not agreement P(o=a) (0.569 vs 0.59 at label 0.7 / auditor 0.8); undefined in the README.

verdict: Every number reproduces: run.py regenerates results.txt byte-for-byte, and an independent reimplementation using the textbook closed-form correction (diag(pi)C = A^-T J) matches all population-limit cells to 4 dp. The method is the right one and the limitations are candid. It misses the bar on verification: the blind baseline and the entire utility model are untested (2 of 4 non-equivalent mutants survive). Fitness is 2 because the bias-and-correction result is the classical imperfect-reference-standard result, which goes uncited; only the translation into utility loss in a round-number model is new. Smaller issues: result 5's mean comparison is within Monte Carlo error, 'implied label accuracy' is undefined, and the Next steps are stale. Not meeting the bar (verification 2); finished (completeness 3).
